prompt: Invent a short myth explaining why the sea is salty, in your own style.

Long ago, when the world was still cooling and the mountains were merely mounds of wet clay, the Ocean was not a sea, but a vast, shimmering lake of distilled sweetness. It tasted of melted snow and starlight, and the creatures that swam within it were made of glass and song.

In those days, the Earth was guarded by a Giant named Oros, whose heart was a single, massive crystal of pure salt. Oros was the keeper of Balance; he ensured that the rains fell in time and that the tides obeyed the moon. He was a lonely sentinel, for his heart was too heavy for him to dance, and too brittle for him to embrace.

Oros fell in love with the Spirit of the Lake, a fluid, shifting entity of sapphire blue who laughed in ripples and spoke in bubbles. For an age, they existed in a fragile harmony—the steadfast mountain of a man and the restless water of a woman. He would tell her stories of the deep earth, and she would sing him songs of the distant horizons.

But the Balance is a jealous master. The Great Void, seeing the warmth between the stone and the water, whispered a lie into Oros’s ear: *“She does not love your stillness. She finds your heart a cold, hard stone, and she longs to be free of your shadow.”*

Consumed by a sudden, jagged grief, Oros did not rage or scream. Instead, he wept. He wept for the love he felt was unrequited, and he wept for the loneliness that had defined his existence since the first dawn. 

As his sorrow grew, the crystal heart within his chest began to fracture under the pressure of his anguish. Finally, with a sound like a thousand breaking mirrors, his heart shattered. The Great Salt Crystal dissolved, pouring out of his chest in a torrential, white river of brine.

The Spirit of the Lake, seeing his heartbreak, rushed forward to embrace him, to wash away the pain and hold him in her cool depths. She absorbed every grain of his sorrow, pulling the salt into her own body so that Oros might be light enough to finally dance.

Oros was freed from his burden and ascended into the stars, becoming the constellations that guide sailors home. But the Spirit of the Lake remained, forever changed. She took the salt of his heart into her veins, turning her sweetness into a brine that remembers the weight of a giant's love.

Long ago, when the world was still wet and the mountains were merely pebbles, the Sky and the Sea were deeply in love. The Sky was a restless spirit of sapphire and gold, while the Sea was a shimmering mirror of silver, stretching endlessly to hold the Sky’s reflection.

They lived in a state of eternal embrace, but they were separated by the Horizon—a strict, invisible border drawn by the Great Architect to keep the heavens from flooding the earth and the waters from drowning the stars.

For eons, they were content to touch only at the edges of the world. But as the ages passed, the Sky grew lonely. He watched the fish dance in the deep and longed to touch the velvet currents of the Sea’s heart. The Sea, in turn, spent her days reaching upward in crashing waves, trying to pull the Sky down into her cool embrace.

One evening, driven by a desperation that shook the foundations of the earth, the Sky leaned down so far that he whispered a secret into the ear of the tide. He promised the Sea that if she could gather every precious thing she owned—every pearl, every shimmering scale, every sunken treasure—and pile them high enough, she could build a bridge to the stars.

The Sea, blinded by love, spent a thousand years scavenging the depths. She clawed at the ocean floor and sifted through the abyssal plains, gathering all the minerals and salts of the earth, piling them into a mountain of white crystal that pierced the clouds.

But the Great Architect saw this defiance. Just as the Sea reached the summit of her crystal mountain, ready to leap into the Sky’s arms, the Architect struck the peak with a bolt of thunder. 

The mountain shattered. 

The great white spire disintegrated into a trillion microscopic grains, dissolving instantly into the water. The bridge was gone, and the lovers were cast back to their respective realms, separated once more by the immutable Horizon.

The Sea wept for her lost bridge and her distant lover. Her tears were fresh, but they fell into a basin already filled with the dissolved ruins of her ambition. To this day, the sea remains salty—not from the earth, but from the dissolved remnants of a bridge built of longing, and the eternal bitterness of a love that almost touched the stars.

Long ago, when the world was still damp from the first rains, the ocean was a mirror of pure, sweet water. It was the domain of Oryn, the Weaver of Tides, a spirit of immense curiosity and a devastatingly clumsy heart.

Oryn lived in a palace of floating glass, but he spent his days enamored with the creatures of the dry land. He loved the way the mountain goats leaped and the way the pine trees smelled of resin. Most of all, he loved the humans, who spent their short lives building things that didn’t wash away.

One day, Oryn decided he wanted to gift the humans a treasure that would last forever. He spent a century scouring the deep trenches of the earth, gathering every crystal of salt he could find. To Oryn, salt was the most precious substance in existence—it was the "stone of preservation," the only thing that could stop time from rotting the world. He gathered it into a single, colossal amphora made of moonlight and pearl, intending to give it to the people so they might preserve their harvests and their memories for eternity.

But as Oryn rose to the surface to deliver his gift, he saw a great storm brewing. He saw a fishing boat tossed like a splinter in the surf, the sailors screaming as they were dragged toward the jagged rocks.

Panic seized the Weaver. In his desperation to reach the boat and pull the sailors to safety, Oryn lunged forward. He forgot the weight of the moonlight jar in his arms. As he dove into the churning foam, the amphora struck a reef and shattered into a billion microscopic shards.

The Great Salt, intended to preserve the world, dissolved instantly into the sweet waters of the deep.

Oryn saved the sailors, but the ocean was changed forever. The sweetness vanished, replaced by a sharp, bracing brine. 

They say that Oryn still weeps for his lost treasure, and that is why the sea continues to rise and fall—the tide is simply the ocean trying to breathe through the weight of a gift that was too heavy for the world to hold.
